response.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT r.name AS name, AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points, COUNT(DISTINCT ds.driverId) AS cnt FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM per_name) SELECT AVG(p.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points, AVG(p.cnt) AS avg_cnt, AVG(p.cnt - o.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM per_name p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.cnt > o.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Race names are grouped exactly as stored in races.name, across all years. The per-name average points is the plain average over all matching driverStandings rows (NULLs ignored). Distinct drivers are counted per race name across all seasons.
The overall average count is the unweighted mean of the per-name distinct-driver counts across all race names that have standings.
